author: Mation
text_post: Easy, killer. What TrueStory was trying to say is that no book is a substitute for learning through the real-life experience of the field. You can read all the theory you want, but if you don't get out there and practice it, it's just useless knowledge accumulated in your head.  Here's another martial arts analogy: (since the forums don't have enough of 'em ) If you read 100 books about martial arts, and you internalize all the information, but you never get out and practice, the first time you step up and spar with a green belt, you'll get your ass kicked. On the other hand, if you read NO books, and you just go out and take an ass-whipping every night, you will get better. You may not use any particular technique correctly, because you haven't had any formal training, but you won't get your ass kicked nearly as often. But if you practice AND learn the theory, then you'll be really learning the art. You will get exponentially better, because in addition to the knowledge you gain from abstract sources, you have real-world, hands on experience to reinforce what you've learned.  The same thing applies to pick-up. Read the material, learn the theory, but get out in the field and learn it first hand, too. The field is BY FAR the best teacher, and they don't sell it on Amazon.  Mation
